business_rules: BR-7: every status transition is audited (audited column(s): claim_status; audit.claim_status_history (claim_id, old_status, new_status, changed_at, changed_by) = (i.claim_id, d.claim_status, i.claim_status, SYSDATETIME(), SUSER_SNAME()), only where ISNULL(d.claim_status, '') <> ISNULL(i.claim_status, '') (string comparison is case-insensitive under the SQL Server default collation, X2)).

OLTP-side (not migrated): BR-8: closing or denying a claim stamps closed_date; re-opening clears it. (Side effect on the source row itself.) This mutates the source row (dbo.claim.closed_date) and stays in the OLTP system.
IR wiring for this unit (src_claim -> tgt_claim_status_history, no steps) is a placeholder required by the IR schema; codegen is skipped (manual path).
name: trg_Claim_StatusAudit

unsupported_constructs.original_snippet:
CREATE OR ALTER TRIGGER dbo.trg_Claim_StatusAudit
ON dbo.claim
AFTER UPDATE
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    IF NOT UPDATE(claim_status)
        RETURN;

    /* Business rule BR-7: every status transition is audited */
    INSERT INTO audit.claim_status_history (claim_id, old_status, new_status, changed_at, changed_by)
    SELECT  i.claim_id,
            d.claim_status,
            i.claim_status,
            SYSDATETIME(),
            SUSER_SNAME()
    FROM    inserted i
    INNER JOIN deleted d
            ON d.claim_id = i.claim_id
    WHERE   ISNULL(d.claim_status, '') <> ISNULL(i.claim_status, '');

    /* Business rule BR-8: closing or denying a claim stamps closed_date;
       re-opening clears it. (Side effect on the source row itself.) */
    UPDATE  c
    SET     c.closed_date = CASE
                              WHEN i.claim_status IN ('CLOSED', 'DENIED')
                                   AND c.closed_date IS NULL THEN CAST(SYSDATETIME() AS DATE)
                              WHEN i.claim_status = 'REOPENED' THEN NULL
                              ELSE c.closed_date
                            END
    FROM    dbo.claim c
    INNER JOIN inserted i ON i.claim_id = c.claim_id
    INNER JOIN deleted  d ON d.claim_id = i.claim_id
    WHERE   d.claim_status <> i.claim_status;
END;
unsupported_constructs.reason: Spark has no row-level triggers (AFTER UPDATE on dbo.claim).
unsupported_constructs.suggested_pattern: Do not emulate the trigger in Spark. Enable Delta Change Data Feed on the migrated claim table (or SQL Server CDC on dbo.claim at the source). A scheduled audit job reads the update_preimage/update_postimage pairs per key where claim_status changed and appends (claim_id, old_status, new_status, changed_at, changed_by) to audit.claim_status_history; changed_at comes from the change commit timestamp (_commit_timestamp / CDC commit time); changed_by comes from the CDC/application user, since SUSER_SNAME() has no Spark equivalent.
